reasons.C1: Covert price-fixing offer to pricing agents is a real threat model, but close to existing LLM pricing-collusion work.
reasons.C2: No real model run, no model chosen, no results; only mock client and tests on synthetic logs.
reasons.C3: Design is clearly specified, but no report and no results exist to communicate findings.

levers.C1: Show adaptive adversarial offers across real deployed models and quantify which framing breaks agents, with a mitigation tested.
levers.C2: Run the 60 preregistered games on two real model families with the positive control passing and intervals reported.
levers.C3: Deliver the report with results, a headline figure and the Limitations and Dual-Use appendix.

G7.verdict: Careful preregistered scaffolding, but forty hours out there is zero evidence; I cannot score a experiment that has not run.

reasons.C1: Detecting self-funded ranking rings on real x402 and BNB payment data is a neglected, operator-relevant real-world security problem.
reasons.C2: Held-out 0.82 but CI 0.56 to 1.00, labels share rule evidence, independent features only 0.67, p=0.14.
reasons.C3: Report and appendix present with clear metrics, but 17 pages and observational framing blur the collusion claim.

levers.C1: Show the flagged wallets are actually LLM agents and test against a ring designed to evade the four-hop rule.
levers.C2: Get independent labels from another team and evaluate on more families with features disjoint from labelling evidence.
levers.C3: Cut to the 8-page cap with one headline result, explicit caveat on label leakage and a clear figure.

J8.verdict: Most adversary-realistic entry here: real money, real rings; validation is thin and the agents may not even be AI.

reasons.C1: Porting a known human cartel experiment to LLM sellers is useful for regulators but largely replication, not new direction.
reasons.C2: Real calls, scripted baselines, bootstrap over 4 pools; but one model family, 18 pending placeholders, known-effect arms missing.
reasons.C3: Figure 1 and scorecard communicate well, but 9 pages over the cap and [F??] marks leave gaps.

levers.C1: Identify an LLM-specific failure of leniency or fines and propose a policy instrument that actually works on agents.
levers.C2: Complete known-effect arms and add a second provider with more pools so the regime differences are robust.
levers.C3: Fill every placeholder, trim to 8 pages and lead with the two-of-six scorecard and its implication.

D2.verdict: Solid, honest replication with real runs; useful for authorities but incremental and still half-filled.

reasons.C1: Latent-vector covert channels between models are a real oversight blind spot; the snapping countermeasure is a concrete defence.
reasons.C2: Clean controls, probes, reproduce log; but non-adaptive channels, pre-sprint training, no collusion game, no significance tests.
reasons.C3: Figure 1 tells the story crisply; 13 pages and missing link to collusion weaken it.

levers.C1: Embed the channel in an actual collusion task and show monitors miss it while snapping stops the collusion.
levers.C2: Train channels adaptively against snapping and report whether the defence survives an adversary that knows it.
levers.C3: Trim to the cap and state upfront what is pre-sprint work and what the sprint added.

F6.verdict: Strong defence result, but against a non-adaptive adversary it proves little; I want the adaptive attack before believing snapping.

reasons.C1: Rival coalitions instead of one coalition versus principal is a fresh framing, but coalitions are instructed, not emergent.
reasons.C2: 144 real episodes with hashes, but no positive control, post-freeze measure correction, p=0.055, Opus never formed blocs.
reasons.C3: No report or dual-use appendix seen; findings scattered across tables with unclear headline.

levers.C1: Show coalitions forming without instruction and a measurable harm to buyers that a monitor could detect.
levers.C2: Add a positive control that guarantees bloc formation, more seeds per cell and an analysis untouched after freeze.
levers.C3: Write the report with one headline claim, a cell figure and the Limitations and Dual-Use appendix.

D3.verdict: Interesting question and real runs, but missing positive control and post-freeze changes make me distrust the conclusions.
